\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{موضوعي} (mawḍūʿī)}{موضوعي (mawḍūʿī)}]{\ar{موضوعي} (mawḍūʿī) — objective}

\label{lesson:AR-C422-mawdui}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for intelligence, then the Arabic for diligence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{موضوعي}}
\textbf{\ar{موضوعي}} — \emph{mawḍūʿī} — \textquotedblleft{}objective\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{الحكم} \ar{موضوعيا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna al-ḥakam mawḍūʿiyyan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The referee was objective.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{موضوعي}} (\emph{mawḍūʿī}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-ḍ-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to put, to lay down\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Mawḍūʿī} is a modern adjective from \emph{mawḍūʿ}, a subject: keeping to the thing itself, objective.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mawḍūʿī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mawḍūʿī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna al-ḥakam mawḍūʿiyyan.} — The referee was objective.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for intelligence, then the Arabic for diligence, then say \emph{mawḍūʿī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{موضوعي} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Objective\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تسامح} (tasāmuḥ)}{تسامح (tasāmuḥ)}]{\ar{تسامح} (tasāmuḥ) — tolerance}

\label{lesson:AR-C422-tasamuh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for diligence, then the Arabic for objective.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تسامح}}
\textbf{\ar{تسامح}} — \emph{tasāmuḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}tolerance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{التسامح} \ar{مهم} \ar{بين} \ar{الجيران}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{at-tasāmuḥ muhimm bayna al-jīrān.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Tolerance is important between neighbours.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تسامح}} (\emph{tasāmuḥ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-m-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be generous, to grant\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Tasāmuḥ} is the Form VI verbal noun, being generous with one another: tolerance. \ar{سامح}, to forgive, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasāmuḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasāmuḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{at-tasāmuḥ muhimm bayna al-jīrān.} — Tolerance is important between neighbours.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for diligence, then the Arabic for objective, then say \emph{tasāmuḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تسامح} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Tolerance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مبرر} (mubarrir)}{مبرر (mubarrir)}]{\ar{مبرر} (mubarrir) — a justification; a pretext}

\label{lesson:AR-C422-mubarrir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for objective, then the Arabic for tolerance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مبرر}}
\textbf{\ar{مبرر}} — \emph{mubarrir} — \textquotedblleft{}a justification; a pretext\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لا} \ar{يوجد} \ar{مبرر} \ar{لهذا} \ar{التأخير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lā yūjadu mubarrir li-hādhā at-taʾkhīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is no justification for this delay.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مبرر}} (\emph{mubarrir}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-r-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to be true, to be good\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Mubarrir} is the Form II active participle, what shows a thing to be right: a justification, a pretext.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mubarrir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mubarrir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lā yūjadu mubarrir li-hādhā at-taʾkhīr.} — There is no justification for this delay.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for objective, then the Arabic for tolerance, then say \emph{mubarrir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مبرر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A justification; a pretext\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{غياب} (ghiyāb)}{غياب (ghiyāb)}]{\ar{غياب} (ghiyāb) — absence}

\label{lesson:AR-C422-ghiyab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for tolerance, then the Arabic for a justification.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{غياب}}
\textbf{\ar{غياب}} — \emph{ghiyāb} — \textquotedblleft{}absence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لاحظ} \ar{المعلم} \ar{غياب} \ar{الطالب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lāḥaẓa al-muʿallim ghiyāb aṭ-ṭālib.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The teacher noticed the student's absence.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{غياب}} (\emph{ghiyāb}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{gh-y-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to be absent, hidden\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ghiyāb} is a verbal noun: being away, absence.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghiyāb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghiyāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lāḥaẓa al-muʿallim ghiyāb aṭ-ṭālib.} — The teacher noticed the student's absence.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for tolerance, then the Arabic for a justification, then say \emph{ghiyāb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{غياب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Absence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استنكر} (istankara)}{استنكر (istankara)}]{\ar{استنكر} (istankara) — to condemn}

\label{lesson:AR-C422-istankara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a justification, then the Arabic for absence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استنكر}}
\textbf{\ar{استنكر}} — \emph{istankara} — \textquotedblleft{}to condemn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استنكر} \ar{الناس} \ar{العنف} \ar{في} \ar{الشارع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istankara an-nās al-ʿunf fī ash-shāriʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People condemned the violence in the street.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستنكر}, \emph{yastankir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استنكر}} (\emph{istankara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-k-r}, \textquotedblleft{}not to know, to deny\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, to hold a thing to be wrong: to condemn.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istankara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istankara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istankara an-nās al-ʿunf fī ash-shāriʿ.} — People condemned the violence in the street.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a justification, then the Arabic for absence, then say \emph{istankara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{استنكر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To condemn\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
